title: Quasi-compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed
statement: Let $T$ be a Hausdorff topological space, meaning that any two distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods. Let $E\subseteq T$ be quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]: every covering of $E$ by sets open in its subspace topology has a finite subcovering. Then $E$ is closed in $T$. No nonemptiness or compactness assumption on $T$ is imposed.

mathlib_match.how: exact: IsCompact.isClosed at line 592 has [T2Space T] and IsCompact E as hypotheses and IsClosed E as conclusion. Mathlib compactness does not impose separation or nonemptiness; T2Space is precisely the Hausdorff condition.
